blocks.source: Physics notation (the dictionary used in every chapter).
The abstract objects of this manuscript translate into standard physics notation as follows; each later chapter adds the translation of its own objects.
• Spacetime.

$V$ is complexified Euclidean $\mathbb R^4$ with indices $m=1,\dots,4$; the Wick map $v^0=-iv^4$ relates it to Minkowski space, and the Euclidean matrices are $\sigma^m_{\alpha\dot\alpha}=(\vec\sigma,i)$, $\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}=(-\vec\sigma,i)$, so that $\sigma^\mu v_\mu=\sigma^mv_m$ for Srednicki's $\sigma^\mu=(1,\vec\sigma)$.
• Four-dimensional spinors.
$S_+$ is the undotted Weyl spinor, index $\alpha=1,2$, Srednicki's left-handed $(2,1)$ of $SU(2)_L\times SU(2)_R$; $S_-$ is the dotted one, index $\dot\alpha$, the $(1,2)$.
This is the assignment for the orientation $dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4$, for which $\rho(e_1e_2e_3e_4)=+1$ on $S_+\otimes W$ (Proposition 1.2).

Indices move with $\varepsilon^{12}=\varepsilon^{\dot1\dot2}=+1$, $\varepsilon_{12}=\varepsilon_{\dot1\dot2}=-1$, and $\chi\psi=\chi^\alpha\psi_\alpha$, $\bar\chi\bar\psi=\bar\chi_{\dot\alpha}\bar\psi^{\dot\alpha}$.
• R-symmetry.
$W=\mathbb C^4$ is the fundamental $\mathbf 4$ of $SU(4)_R\cong\mathrm{Spin}(6)$, written with an upper index $w^i$; $W^*$ is the $\bar{\mathbf 4}$, lower index $w_i$.

The six transverse directions $W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$ are the vector $\mathbf 6$ of $SO(6)_R$ with components $w_I$, $I=1,\dots,6$, equivalently the antisymmetric $\mathbf 6$ of $SU(4)$: $w_{ij}=w_I\Sigma^I_{ij}$ with the 't Hooft blocks $\Sigma^I$, $w^{ij}=\tfrac12\varepsilon^{ijkl}w_{kl}$, which is the complex conjugate of $w_{ij}$ for real $w$, and $(u,w)=\tfrac14u^{ij}w_{ij}$.
The six scalars $\iota_wA$ are $A_I$ in the $SO(6)$ form and $A_{ij}=A_I\Sigma^I_{ij}$ in the $SU(4)$ form, with $\iota_wA=\tfrac14w^{ij}A_{ij}$.
• Ten-dimensional spinors.
$V_{10}=V\oplus W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$ carries the index $M=(m,I)$.
$\Sigma$ is a Weyl spinor $\mathbf{16}$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ and $\Sigma^*$ the other one, $\mathbf{16}'$.
Writing an element of $\Sigma$ with a lower index, $\zeta_A$, and an element of $\Sigma^*$ with an upper index, $\chi^A$ ($A=1,\dots,16$), the reduction to $SU(2)_L\times SU(2)_R\times SU(4)$ is

\zeta_A=\big(\xi_\alpha{}^i,\ \bar\xi_{\dot\alpha i}\big)\in(\mathbf 2,\mathbf 1,\mathbf 4)\oplus(\mathbf 1,\mathbf 2,\bar{\mathbf 4}),\qquad \chi^A=\big(\eta^\alpha{}_i,\ \bar\eta^{\dot\alpha i}\big)\in(\mathbf 2,\mathbf 1,\bar{\mathbf 4})\oplus(\mathbf 1,\mathbf 2,\mathbf 4):
on $\Sigma$ the spinor indices are lower and the $SU(4)$ index is upper on the $\mathbf 4$, lower on the $\bar{\mathbf 4}$; on $\Sigma^*$ all positions are reversed.

The pairing $\Sigma\otimes\Sigma^*\to\mathbb C$ is $(\zeta,\chi)=\xi_\alpha{}^i\eta^\alpha{}_i-\bar\xi_{\dot\alpha i}\bar\eta^{\dot\alpha i}$, the minus sign on the dotted block being part of the convention of [ESW].
• Gamma matrices.

$\rho(v)=v^M\Gamma_M$ is Clifford multiplication by the ten-dimensional gamma matrices in their chiral blocks, $\Gamma_M\colon\Sigma\to\Sigma^*$ and $\Sigma^*\to\Sigma$, with $\Gamma_M\Gamma_N+\Gamma_N\Gamma_M=2\delta_{MN}$; the $\Gamma$-pairing $\Gamma(\zeta_1,\zeta_2)^M=(\rho(e^M)\zeta_1,\zeta_2)$ is the symmetric bilinear $\zeta_1\Gamma^M\zeta_2$.

Along spacetime, on the Dirac column $(\psi_\alpha,\bar\chi^{\dot\alpha})$, $\rho(v)=\gamma_W^\mu v_\mu=-i\gamma_S^\mu v_\mu$ with Weinberg's and Srednicki's gamma matrices after the Wick map; in components $(\rho(v)\xi)^\alpha{}_i=i\,v_m\bar\xi_{\dot\alpha i}\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}$ and $(\rho(v)\xi)^{\dot\alpha i}=-i\,v_m\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}\xi_\alpha{}^i$.

Along $W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$, $\rho(w)$ is the Yukawa matrix, $(\rho(w)\xi)^\alpha{}_j=\varepsilon^{\alpha\beta}w_{ji}\xi_\beta{}^i$, $(\rho(w)\xi)^{\dot\alpha j}=\varepsilon^{\dot\alpha\dot\beta}w^{ji}\bar\xi_{\dot\beta i}$.

On a two-form, $\rho(F)=\rho(q(F))$ is $\tfrac12F_{MN}\Gamma^{MN}$ with $\Gamma^{MN}$ the antisymmetrised product, and ${\not d}_A=\Gamma^MD_M$ reduces to the four-dimensional Dirac operator $\bar\sigma^mD_m$ plus the Yukawa couplings $[A_{ij},-]$.
• Parities and ghost numbers.

$\Pi$ is the parity shift: $\Pi\Sigma\otimes\mathfrak g$ means that the gaugino components $\lambda_\alpha{}^i$, $\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}$ are Grassmann-odd fields of ghost number $0$, four left-handed Weyl fermions in the $\mathbf 4$ and their right-handed partners in the $\bar{\mathbf 4}$; in Euclidean signature $\bar\lambda$ is an independent field, which on a Lorentzian real slice is Srednicki's $\lambda^\dagger$.
$\mathfrak g[1]$ places the ghost $c$ in degree $-1$ as a section, so its coordinate has ghost number $+1$.
The ghost numbers of the coordinates are $c:+1$, $A,\lambda:0$, $A^*,\lambda^*:-1$, $c^*:-2$, and the Grassmann parities are odd for $c,\lambda,A^*$ and even for $A,\lambda^*,c^*$.
The gaugino antifield has components $\lambda^{*\alpha}{}_i$, $\bar\lambda^{*\dot\alpha i}$ in $\Sigma^*$.
• Gauge algebra and coupling.

The coupling sits in the pairing of $\mathfrak g$: for $\mathfrak{su}(N)$, $(X,Y)=-\tfrac{4\hbar}{g^2}\operatorname{tr}(XY)$, and with $A_m=-igA^a_mT^a$, $A_I=-igA^a_IT^a$, $\lambda=-\tfrac{ig}{\sqrt2}\lambda^aT^a$, $\operatorname{tr}(T^aT^b)=\tfrac12\delta^{ab}$, $S/\hbar$ is the Wick image of Srednicki's Lagrangian $-\tfrac14F^{a\mu\nu}F^a_{\mu\nu}-\tfrac12D^\mu A_ID_\mu A_I+i\lambda^{\dagger a}\bar\sigma^\mu D_\mu\lambda^a+\cdots$; the unit $\frac{\hbar\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y)}{16\pi^2(X,Y)}$ equals $-\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}$.
• Superconformal generators.

The odd generators of $\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)$ in the blocks of [SW, (17)] are $Q^i_\alpha$, $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha i}$ (parameters $\xi_\alpha{}^i$, $\bar\xi_{\dot\alpha i}$, an element of $\Sigma$) and $S^\alpha{}_i$, $\bar S^{\dot\alpha i}$ (parameters $\eta^\alpha{}_i$, $\bar\eta^{\dot\alpha i}$, an element of $\Sigma^*$); the even part consists of $P_m$, $K_m$, the dilatation $\Delta=2E$ of [SW, (17)] (the physics dilatation is $D=-E=-\tfrac12\Delta$, the generator $-E$ of [SW, (3)], with $[D,P_m]=P_m$), the rotations $\mathfrak{so}(4)=\mathfrak{su}(2)_L\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)_R$ and the R-symmetry $\mathfrak{so}(6)=\mathfrak{su}(4)$.
Physics notation (fields, action and propagator).
In the components of the physics notation key after Section 1.2:

• $x^m$, $m=1,\dots,4$, are the coordinates of Euclidean $\mathbb R^4$; $W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$ carries the $SO(6)_R$ vector index $I=1,\dots,6$ and $W$, the $\mathbf 4$ of $SU(4)_R$, the index $i=1,\dots,4$.

• $A|_V=A_m$ is the gauge field, $\iota_wA=w_IA_I$ the six scalars, $\lambda=(\lambda_\alpha{}^i,\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i})$ the four gauginos, $c$ the Faddeev–Popov ghost, and $A^*_m$, $A^*_I$, $\lambda^{*\alpha}{}_i$, $\bar\lambda^{*\dot\alpha i}$, $c^*$ the antifields, all $\mathfrak g$-valued.
• $S$ is the BV action of Euclidean $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang–Mills theory with weight $e^{S/\hbar}$, $Q$ its linearised BRST operator, $I$ the interaction and $\{-,-\}$ the BV antibracket.

• $Q^{GF}$ is the Feynman-gauge gauge-fixing operator, $H=-\partial_m\partial_m$ ($|p|^2$ in momentum space), $K_t$ the heat kernel with momentum factor $e^{-t|p|^2}$, and $P(\varepsilon,\infty)$ the Feynman-gauge propagator with proper-time cutoff $\varepsilon$ (mass dimension $-2$): each component is its fibre factor times $\int_\varepsilon^\infty e^{-t|p|^2}dt=e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}/|p|^2$.

For $\mathfrak{su}(N)$, with $A_M=-igA^a_MT^a$, $M=(m,I)$, and $\lambda=-\tfrac{ig}{\sqrt2}\lambda^aT^a$, the edge $\hbar P(\varepsilon,\infty)$ of $\hbar\partial_{P(\varepsilon,\infty)}$ is the canonical Euclidean propagator of the gluon, the six scalars and the gauginos, written out in components after Proposition 3.11.

• $W(P,J)$ is $\hbar$ times the sum of connected Feynman graphs with edges $\hbar P$ and vertices $J/\hbar$, each graph weighted by $\hbar$ to its number of loops; $\varepsilon^{-1}$ and $\log\varepsilon$ are the quadratic and logarithmic divergences.

• With $\omega=f\,d^4x$, $\int\omega\,(\iota_{w_1}A,\iota_{w_2}A)=w_{1I}w_{2J}\int d^4x\,f\,(A_I,A_J)$, equal to $2\hbar\,w_{1I}w_{2J}\int d^4x\,f\,A^a_IA^a_J$ for $\mathfrak{su}(N)$; $\delta$ is its source, $O(\varepsilon)$ the bare operator including its counterterm, and $O[\infty]$ the renormalised operator.

• $\Delta=2E=2x^m\partial_m$, and $[(d_{CE}+Q)O[\infty]](x_1)$ is the quantum-corrected transformation of $O$ along the generator $x_1$ of the key: $P_m$, $K_m$, $\Delta$, rotations, R-symmetry, $Q^i_\alpha$, $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha i}$, $S^\alpha{}_i$, $\bar S^{\dot\alpha i}$.
Physics notation (the UV boundary).

• $K_0$ is $-\delta^4(x-y)$ times the inverse fibre pairing on each field–antifield pair; $K_t$ has $\delta^4(x-y)$ replaced by $(4\pi t)^{-2}e^{-|x-y|^2/4t}$, momentum factor $e^{-t|p|^2}$, so $K_\infty=0$ and $K_\varepsilon-K_0$ carries the factor $e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}-1$.
• $L_t=(Q^{GF}\otimes1)K_t$ is the integrand of the proper-time representation $P(\varepsilon,\infty)=\int_\varepsilon^\infty L_t\,dt$: the fibre factor of the propagator times $e^{-t|p|^2}$.

• $P(0,\infty)$ is the Feynman-gauge propagator without cutoff, fibre factor times $1/|p|^2$, and $Q\,P(0,\infty)\star+P(0,\infty)\star\,Q=1$ makes $P(0,\infty)\star$ a Green's operator of the free BRST operator $Q$.

• $\Delta_\varepsilon=-\partial_{K_\varepsilon}$ is the BV Laplacian regularised by the heat kernel at proper time $\varepsilon$; the quantum master equation at the UV boundary reads $(d_{CE}+Q)J+\tfrac12\{J,J\}_\varepsilon+\hbar\Delta_\varepsilon J=0$, with classical part the Zinn-Justin equation.
• The $\varepsilon^{-1}$ mass terms are $(A_m,A_m)+(A_I,A_I)$, and the finite counterterm forced by the master equation is $(\partial_mA_m,\partial_nA_n)$ (Section 0.4).
Physics notation (the objects of the chapters).

The Feynman-gauge operator $Q^{GF}$ of Chapter 3, written out in components after Definition 3.1, maps the antifield $A^*_M$ to $-2A^*_M$ in the slot of $A_M$ and $A_m$ to $\partial_mA_m$ in the ghost slot, with $H=[Q,Q^{GF}]=-\partial_m\partial_m$.

The single letters are $\int\omega\,(X,A_I)$, $\int\omega\,(X,v_mA_m)$, $\int\omega\,(\zeta,\lambda)$, $\int\omega\,(X,c)$; the scalar bilinears are $w_{1I}w_{2J}\int\omega\,(A_I,A_J)$, whose traceless part is the $\mathbf{20'}$ of $SU(4)_R$ and whose trace $\int\omega\,(A_I,A_I)$ is the Konishi operator.
The other superconformal components of Chapter 7 are those along $Q^i_\alpha$, $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha i}$, $S^\alpha{}_i$, $\bar S^{\dot\alpha i}$ and $K_m$.
Physics notation (the results of Step 1).
With $(A_I,A_I)=\tfrac14(A^{ij},A_{ij})$, $F^0_{mn}=\partial_mA_n-\partial_nA_m$ and $d^*A|_V=-\partial_mA_m$, the quadratic counterterm of Chapter 4 is
gauge-boson and scalar mass terms at order $\varepsilon^{-1}$ and kinetic terms at order $\log\varepsilon$.
The $\log\varepsilon$ part through quartic order is the unit times $\log\varepsilon\,(Q+\{I,-\})$ of
\int d^4x\Big\{2(A_m,A^*_m)+2(A_I,A^*_I)-4\big[(\lambda_\alpha{}^i,\lambda^{*\alpha}{}_i)-(\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i},\bar\lambda^{*\dot\alpha i})\big]-(c^*,c)\Big\},
the BV form of a wave-function renormalisation, with vanishing one-loop beta function of $g$.
The finite counterterm is $-\tfrac{27}{16}$ units times $\int d^4x\,(\partial_mA_m,\partial_nA_n)$, removing the obstruction $-\tfrac{27}{8}$ units times $\int d^4x\,(\partial^2c,\partial_mA_m)$.

In Chapters 5 and 6, $(\zeta,\lambda)=(\lambda_\alpha{}^i,\zeta^\alpha{}_i)-(\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i},\bar\zeta^{\dot\alpha i})$, $(w_1,w_2)=w_{1I}w_{2I}$, the traceless bilinear is the $\mathbf{20'}$ and the trace $\int\omega\,(A_I,A_I)=-\tfrac{4\hbar}{g^2}\int\omega\operatorname{tr}(A_IA_I)$ the Konishi operator.

In the item on Chapter 6, the generator written $\Delta=-E$ of [SW, (3)] is $-E=-\tfrac12\Delta$, the physics dilatation $D$ with $[D,P_m]=P_m$; the manuscript's $\Delta$ is the generator $2E$ of [SW, (17)].

The coefficient times the unit is the one-loop anomalous dimension, and $w_O$ plus it the scaling dimension; for $\mathfrak{su}(N)$ the table gives the anomalous dimensions $0$ for the $\mathbf{20'}$, $\tfrac{3g^2N}{4\pi^2}$ for the Konishi operator and, in Feynman gauge, $\tfrac{g^2N}{8\pi^2}$ for $A_I$ and $A_m$, $\tfrac{g^2N}{4\pi^2}$ for $\lambda$, $\tfrac{g^2N}{16\pi^2}$ for $c$.
Physics notation (Clifford relation, Gamma-pairing and Dirac operator).
In the two-component notation of the physics notation key after Section 1.2, the Clifford relation along $V$ and along $W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$ reads
\sigma^m\bar\sigma^n+\sigma^n\bar\sigma^m=-2\delta^{mn},\qquad u^{ik}w_{kj}+w^{ik}u_{kj}=-2(u,w)\,\delta^i_j\quad(u,w\in W_{\mathbb R}^\perp),
and the $\Gamma$-pairing on $\Sigma$ and on $\Sigma^*$ has the components
with $\Gamma_{kl}=\Gamma^I\Sigma^I_{kl}$, $\Gamma^{kl}=\tfrac12\varepsilon^{klij}\Gamma_{ij}$ and $(\Gamma,u)=\Gamma^mu_m+\tfrac14\Gamma_{ij}u^{ij}$.
On two-forms along $V$,

\rho(q(e_m\wedge e_n))\colon\quad \xi_\alpha{}^i\mapsto-\tfrac12(\sigma^m\bar\sigma^n-\sigma^n\bar\sigma^m)_\alpha{}^\beta\xi_\beta{}^i,\qquad \bar\xi_{\dot\alpha i}\mapsto\tfrac12\bar\xi_{\dot\beta i}(\bar\sigma^m\sigma^n-\bar\sigma^n\sigma^m)^{\dot\beta}{}_{\dot\alpha}.
Further $d=dx^m\partial_m$, $\mathrm{dvol}=d^4x$, $(d^*dA)_n=-\partial_m\partial_mA_n+\partial_n\partial_mA_m$ on one-forms, and the Dirac operators are
Physics notation (four-dimensional chirality).

$\mathrm{Spin}(4,\mathbb C)=SL(2,\mathbb C)\times SL(2,\mathbb C)$ is the complexification of $SU(2)_L\times SU(2)_R$, and $\mathrm{Spin}(6,\mathbb C)\cong SL(4,\mathbb C)$ that of $SU(4)_R$, with $W=S_+^6$ the $\mathbf 4$.
The eigenspaces of Proposition 1.2 are
+1:\ \ \xi_\alpha{}^i\in S_+\otimes W,\quad \eta^\alpha{}_i\in S_+\otimes W^*;\qquad -1:\ \ \bar\xi_{\dot\alpha i}\in S_-\otimes W^*,\quad \bar\eta^{\dot\alpha i}\in S_-\otimes W .
On the Dirac column $(\xi_\alpha{}^i,\bar\eta^{\dot\alpha i})$ at fixed $i$,
\rho(e_m)=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\sigma^m\\-i\bar\sigma^m&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \rho(e_1)\rho(e_2)\rho(e_3)\rho(e_4)=-\gamma_{5S}=\gamma_{5W}=\mathrm{diag}(1,1,-1,-1),
so the eigenvalue $+1$ is Srednicki's left-handed chirality and Weinberg's $\gamma_5=+1$.

In indices, $\rho(v)$ exchanges undotted and dotted indices and keeps the position of the $SU(4)$ index, $\xi_\alpha{}^i\mapsto(\rho(v)\xi)^{\dot\alpha i}$; $\rho(w)$ keeps the spinor type and maps the $\mathbf 4$ to the $\bar{\mathbf 4}$ through $w_{ji}$, $\xi_\alpha{}^i\mapsto(\rho(w)\xi)^\alpha{}_j$, and the $\bar{\mathbf 4}$ to the $\mathbf 4$ through $w^{ji}$.
The opposite orientation exchanges dotted and undotted indices in all four eigenspaces.
Physics notation (components of the fields and antifields).
Under $SU(2)_L\times SU(2)_R\times SU(4)_R$:
• $c$: the Faddeev–Popov ghost, a singlet.

• $A$: $A_M=(A_m,A_I)$, the gauge field $A_m\in(\mathbf 2,\mathbf 2,\mathbf 1)$ and the six scalars $A_I\in(\mathbf 1,\mathbf 1,\mathbf 6)$, with $A_{ij}=A_I\Sigma^I_{ij}$ and $A^{ij}=\tfrac12\varepsilon^{ijkl}A_{kl}$.
• $\lambda$: $\lambda_\alpha{}^i\in(\mathbf 2,\mathbf 1,\mathbf 4)$ and $\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}\in(\mathbf 1,\mathbf 2,\bar{\mathbf 4})$.

• Antifields: $A^*_M=(A^*_m,A^*_I)$ with $A^*_{ij}=A^*_I\Sigma^I_{ij}$, $A^{*ij}=\tfrac12\varepsilon^{ijkl}A^*_{kl}$; $\lambda^{*\alpha}{}_i\in(\mathbf 2,\mathbf 1,\bar{\mathbf 4})$ and $\bar\lambda^{*\dot\alpha i}\in(\mathbf 1,\mathbf 2,\mathbf 4)$; $c^*$, a singlet.
The identifications of duals give the fibre pairings, with $(-,-)$ on $\mathfrak g$ kept on the colour factors,
Physics notation (the BV symplectic form).
With $\mathrm{dvol}=d^4x$,
and $\langle A^*,A\rangle$, $\langle\lambda,\lambda^*\rangle$, $\langle c,c^*\rangle$ are their negatives.

The field–antifield pairs are $(A_m,A^*_m)$, $(A_I,A^*_I)$, $(\lambda_\alpha{}^i,\lambda^{*\alpha}{}_i)$, $(\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i},\bar\lambda^{*\dot\alpha i})$, the last with the sign $-1$, and $(c,c^*)$; the even members $A_M$, $\lambda^{*\alpha}{}_i$, $\bar\lambda^{*\dot\alpha i}$, $c^*$ are the Grassmann-even coordinates.
Physics notation (kernel of the identity, antibracket and BV Laplacian).

With $\delta(x-y)=\delta^4(x-y)$, the components of $K_0$ are $-\delta(x-y)\,\delta_{MN}(-,-)^{-1}$ on $A_M\otimes A^*_N$ and $A^*_N\otimes A_M$, $-\delta(x-y)\,(-,-)^{-1}$ on $c\otimes c^*$ and $c^*\otimes c$, and on $\lambda\otimes\lambda^*$ and $\lambda^*\otimes\lambda$ $-\delta(x-y)\,(-,-)^{-1}$ times the canonical element of $\Sigma\otimes\Sigma^*$, whose components are $\delta_\alpha^\beta\delta^i_j$ between $\lambda_\alpha{}^i$ and $\lambda^{*\beta}{}_j$ and $-\delta_{\dot\alpha}^{\dot\beta}\delta_i^j$ between $\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}$ and $\bar\lambda^{*\dot\beta j}$.
Further, $\{-,-\}$ is the BV antibracket and $\Delta_0=-\partial_{K_0}$ the BV Laplacian, which contracts a field with its antifield at coincident points.
Physics notation (the action in components).
With $D_m=\partial_m+[A_m,-]$, the components of $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$ are
F_{mn}=\partial_mA_n-\partial_nA_m+[A_m,A_n],\qquad (F_A)_{mI}=D_mA_I,\qquad (F_A)_{IJ}=[A_I,A_J],
and $(F_A,F_A)=\sum_{M<N}(F_{MN},F_{MN})$, so that
-\tfrac14(F_A,F_A)=-\tfrac18(F_{mn},F_{mn})-\tfrac14(D_mA_I,D_mA_I)-\tfrac18([A_I,A_J],[A_I,A_J]),
summed over $m,n,I,J$.
The density of (1.1) is

For $\mathfrak{su}(N)$ in the normalisation of the key, with $[T^a,T^b]=if^{abc}T^c$, $A^a_{ij}=A^a_I\Sigma^I_{ij}$, $A^{a\,ij}=\tfrac12\varepsilon^{ijkl}A^a_{kl}$ and Srednicki's contractions, the scalar potential and the Yukawa terms of $S/\hbar$ are
-\tfrac{g^2}4f^{abe}f^{cde}A^a_IA^b_JA^c_IA^d_J-\tfrac g2f^{abc}A^b_{ji}\big(\lambda^{aj}\lambda^{ci}\big)-\tfrac g2f^{abc}A^{b\,ji}\big(\bar\lambda^a_j\bar\lambda^c_i\big).
Physics notation (free part, Fourier convention and real slice).
Up to total derivatives, [(1.2)](#b-00125) is

\tfrac12\langle e,Qe\rangle=\int d^4x\Big\{-\tfrac18(F^0_{mn},F^0_{mn})-\tfrac14(\partial_mA_I,\partial_mA_I)+i\big(\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i},\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}\partial_m\lambda_\alpha{}^i\big)+(\partial_mc,A^*_m)\Big\},
with $F^0_{mn}=\partial_mA_n-\partial_nA_m$.

The coefficient $-\tfrac14$ of Proposition 1.9 gives $-\tfrac18(F_{mn},F_{mn})$, which for $\mathfrak{su}(N)$ is $-\tfrac14F^a_{mn}F^a_{mn}$ in $S/\hbar$; $S^{(1)}(Q_1)$ is the supersymmetry term of the equivariant action, in components at the end of Section 2.3.
The Fourier convention is $e^{i(p,x)}=e^{ip_mx_m}$, so $\partial_m\mapsto ip_m$ and $|p|^2=p_mp_m$.

On the real slice of Remark 1.10 the components $A^a_m$, $A^a_I$ of $A_M=-igA^a_MT^a$ are real and the complex conjugate of $A^a_{ij}$ is $A^{a\,ij}$; the eigenvalue $-\tfrac12|p|^2$ belongs to the three transverse components of $A_m$ and the six $A_I$, the eigenvalue $0$ to $A_m\propto p_m$.
Physics notation (the linearised BRST operator).
With the slot of the image in brackets and $\partial^2=\partial_m\partial_m$,
c\mapsto-\partial_mc\ [A_m],\quad A_m\mapsto\tfrac12(\partial^2A_m-\partial_m\partial_nA_n)\ [A^*_m],\quad A_I\mapsto\tfrac12\partial^2A_I\ [A^*_I],\quad A^*_m\mapsto-\partial_mA^*_m\ [c^*],

\lambda_\alpha{}^i\mapsto-i\,\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}\partial_m\lambda_\alpha{}^i\ [\bar\lambda^{*\dot\alpha i}],\qquad \bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}\mapsto i\,\partial_m\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}\ [\lambda^{*\alpha}{}_i],

in momentum space with $\partial_m\mapsto ip_m$: the linearised gauge transformation $-\partial_mc$, the Maxwell and Klein–Gordon operators of $A_m$ and $A_I$, the Weyl operators of $\lambda_\alpha{}^i$ and $\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}$, and the divergence $-\partial_mA^*_m$ in the $c^*$ slot.
Physics notation (the vertices in components).
Summed over $m,n,I,J$, the terms of [(1.3)](#b-00159) are
-\tfrac12\big(dA,\tfrac12[A\wedge A]\big)=-\tfrac12(\partial_mA_n,[A_m,A_n])-\tfrac12(\partial_mA_I,[A_m,A_I]),
-\tfrac14\big(\tfrac12[A\wedge A],\tfrac12[A\wedge A]\big)=-\tfrac18([A_m,A_n],[A_m,A_n])-\tfrac14([A_m,A_I],[A_m,A_I])-\tfrac18([A_I,A_J],[A_I,A_J]),
([A,c],A^*)=([A_m,c],A^*_m)+([A_I,c],A^*_I),\qquad ([c,\lambda],\lambda^*)=([c,\lambda_\alpha{}^i],\lambda^{*\alpha}{}_i)-([c,\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}],\bar\lambda^{*\dot\alpha i}).
In the vertex functions $\iota_pA(p_j)=p_mA_m(p_j)$, $[A(p_1),A(p_2)]=[A_n(p_1),A_n(p_2)]+[A_I(p_1),A_I(p_2)]$, and the $\lambda\lambda A$ vertex is the gauge coupling plus the Yukawa coupling,
The $r_j$ are Grassmann-odd sources for the legs $\lambda$, $c$ and $A^*$.
Physics notation (gauge transformations and the master equation).
The gauge transformations of the proof of Proposition [1.14](#b-00173) are, in components,
A_m\mapsto D_mc,\qquad A_I\mapsto[A_I,c],\qquad \lambda_\alpha{}^i\mapsto[c,\lambda_\alpha{}^i],\qquad \bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}\mapsto[c,\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}],\qquad c\mapsto\tfrac12[c,c],

the coefficients of $A^*_m$, $A^*_I$, $\lambda^{*\alpha}{}_i$, $-\bar\lambda^{*\dot\alpha i}$ and $c^*$ in the action; $\{S,S\}=0$ is the classical BV master equation (Zinn-Justin equation) and $QI+\tfrac12\{I,I\}=0$ its interacting part.
The functionals of the proof are

\int d^4x\,\big(\lambda,\rho([dc,\lambda])\big)=i\int d^4x\Big\{\big(\lambda_\alpha{}^i,\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}[\partial_mc,\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}]\big)+\big(\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i},\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}[\partial_mc,\lambda_\alpha{}^i]\big)\Big\},
\int d^4x\,\big(df,\Gamma(s_1,s_2)\big)=\int d^4x\,\partial_mf\,\Gamma^m(s_1,s_2),\qquad \int d^4x\,([dc,c],A^*)=\int d^4x\,([\partial_mc,c],A^*_m).
Physics notation (conformal and R-symmetry generators).
The even generators are the vector fields $v^m(x)\partial_m$, with $X_{mn}=\partial_mv_n-\partial_nv_m$:
• translation $P_b$: $v^m=b^m$, so $P_m=\partial_m$;

On the fields, $v.$ is the two-component transformation of $S^{(1)}(v)$ written out after Definition 2.12: the conformal transformation of the vector $A_m$, of the scalars $A_{ij}$ of dimension $1$, of the Weyl spinors $\lambda_\alpha{}^i$, $\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}$ of dimension $\tfrac32$ and of the ghost $c$ of dimension $0$, with the spin term $-\tfrac18X_{mn}(\sigma^m\bar\sigma^n)_\alpha{}^\beta$ on $\lambda_\alpha{}^i$ and the $SU(4)_R$ rotation $r^i{}_j=\tfrac14R_{IJ}(\bar\Sigma^J\Sigma^I)^i{}_j$, traceless and anti-Hermitian for real $R$.

In components the dilatation and the special conformal field along $b$, $v^m=x^2b^m-2(b\cdot x)x^m$, have the data $X_{mn}$, $\operatorname{div}v$ written out after Definition 2.1.

$Q_1\in S_+\otimes W$ is a combination of the supercharges $Q^i_\alpha$, in $(\mathbf2,\mathbf1,\mathbf4)$, and $Q_1\in S_-\otimes W^*$ of the $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha i}$, in $(\mathbf1,\mathbf2,\bar{\mathbf4})$.

Physics notation (special supersymmetry and large distance).
$Q_2\in\Sigma^*$ is a combination of the special supercharges $S^\alpha{}_i$, in $(\mathbf2,\mathbf1,\bar{\mathbf4})$, and $\bar S^{\dot\alpha i}$, in $(\mathbf1,\mathbf2,\mathbf4)$.

The multiplication operator $x\mapsto\Gamma(\rho(x)Q_2,-)$ is that of the conformal Killing spinor written out after Definition 2.2, at $\xi=\bar\xi=0$, linear in $x$: the special supersymmetry transformations of the fields are position dependent, and this multiplication operator fails to commute with $H=-\partial^2$.

In Remark 7.12 the coefficients grow as $|x|$ for $\Delta$ and for $S^\alpha{}_i$, $\bar S^{\dot\alpha i}$, and as $|x|^2$ for $K_b$; the decay $|y|^{-4}$ of a $K_b$ insertion is the borderline of a logarithmic divergence at large distance.
Physics notation (dimensional analysis of the components).
The proposition is dimensional analysis together with ghost-number conservation, gauge invariance and $SO(4)\times SU(4)_R$ covariance.

The value of the conformal Killing spinor ($\xi$ at $x_0=0$) has mass dimension $-\tfrac12$ and its Dirac derivative ($4\eta$) dimension $+\tfrac12$, so the transformation under $Q$ has dimension $w_O+\tfrac12$ and the $\eta$-term dimension $w_O-\tfrac12$; a translation parameter has dimension $-1$, rotation and dilatation parameters $0$, and the special conformal parameter $b$ dimension $+1$.
In components the conformal Killing spinor (8.2) satisfies

\partial_m\epsilon_\alpha{}^i=-i\,\sigma^m_{\alpha\dot\alpha}\bar\eta^{\dot\alpha i},\qquad \partial_m\bar\epsilon_{\dot\alpha i}=i\,\eta^\alpha{}_i\sigma^m_{\alpha\dot\alpha},\qquad i\,\partial_m\bar\epsilon_{\dot\alpha i}\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}=4\eta^\alpha{}_i,\qquad -i\,\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}\partial_m\epsilon_\alpha{}^i=4\bar\eta^{\dot\alpha i},
the last two being the components of ${\not d}(Q_1+\rho(x)Q_2)=4Q_2$.
Physics notation (structures of the one-loop supersymmetry variation).

For $O=4\hbar\,w_{1I}w_{2J}\int\omega\operatorname{tr}(\phi_I\phi_J)$ the one-loop transformation under $Q$ is a dimension-$\tfrac52$ combination of structures with the fields $A_I\lambda$ (classical type), $A_m\lambda$ (gauge-variant type) and $c\lambda^*$ (BRST type).
In two-component form, with the colour pairing between the two $\mathfrak g$-valued factors, for $Q^i_\alpha$, $Q_1=(\xi_\alpha{}^i,0)$,

(\rho(w)Q_1,\lambda)=w_{ji}\,\xi_\alpha{}^j\varepsilon^{\alpha\beta}\lambda_\beta{}^i,\qquad (\rho(v)Q_1,\lambda)=i\,v_m\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}\xi_\alpha{}^i,\qquad (Q_1,\lambda^*)=\xi_\alpha{}^i\lambda^{*\alpha}{}_i,
and for $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha i}$, $Q_1=(0,\bar\xi_{\dot\alpha i})$,

with $w_{ji}\to A_{ji}$, $w^{kl}\to A^{kl}$ for $\rho(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})$ and $v_m\to A_m$ for $\rho(A|_V)$; $(\rho(w)Q_1,\lambda)=\iota_w\Gamma(Q_1,\lambda)=\tfrac14w^{kl}\Gamma_{kl}(Q_1,\lambda)$.

In $SU(4)_R$ language, $\mathbf4\otimes\bar{\mathbf4}=\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf{15}$, $\wedge^2\mathbf6=\mathbf{15}$ (the adjoint) and $\mathrm{Sym}^2\mathbf6=\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf{20'}$, and $\mathbf{20'}$ does not occur in $\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf{15}$.

For $S^\alpha{}_i$ the Killing spinor at $x$ is $\bar\epsilon_{\dot\alpha i}(x)=i\,x_m\eta^\alpha{}_i\sigma^m_{\alpha\dot\alpha}\in S_-\otimes W^*$, and for $\bar S^{\dot\alpha i}$ it is $\epsilon_\alpha{}^i(x)=-i\,x_m\sigma^m_{\alpha\dot\alpha}\bar\eta^{\dot\alpha i}\in S_+\otimes W$.

Order $\hbar^2$ is two loops, order $g^4$ in the normalisation of Remark 6.13.

With $\zeta_A=(\xi_\alpha{}^i,\bar\xi_{\dot\alpha i})\in\Sigma=\mathbf{16}$ and $\chi^A=(\eta^\alpha{}_i,\bar\eta^{\dot\alpha i})\in\Sigma^*=\mathbf{16}'$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ (the key after Section 1.2), the gamma matrices $\Gamma_m=\rho(e_m)$ are the formulas of the definition at $v=e_m$, and the six transverse ones $\Gamma_I=\rho(e_I)$ are, with $\bar\Sigma^I=(\Sigma^I)^\dagger$ and $w^{ij}=-w_I\bar\Sigma^{I\,ij}$,

The 't Hooft blocks are the chiral blocks of the $SO(6)_R$ gamma matrices: on $W\oplus W^*$,

The generators $Q^i_\alpha$, $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha i}$, $S^\alpha{}_i$, $\bar S^{\dot\alpha i}$ span $(\mathbf2,\mathbf1,\mathbf4)$, $(\mathbf1,\mathbf2,\bar{\mathbf4})$, $(\mathbf2,\mathbf1,\bar{\mathbf4})$, $(\mathbf1,\mathbf2,\mathbf4)$ of $SU(2)_L\times SU(2)_R\times SU(4)_R$.

The propagator is that of Feynman gauge: the edges $\hbar P(\varepsilon,T)$ of the flow are the canonical Euclidean propagators written out after Proposition 3.11, with the factor $e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}/|p|^2$ replaced by $\big(e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}-e^{-T|p|^2}\big)/|p|^2$, the modes of proper time between the ultraviolet cutoff $\varepsilon$ and the endpoint $T$ of the transfer of [C07], a Wilsonian scale.

On the unit elements of Definition [8.1](#c8-01405), the odd–odd brackets of Chapter 2 (graded brackets, $P_m=\partial_m$) are
[Q^i_\alpha,\bar Q_{\dot\alpha j}]=i\,\delta^i_j\,\bar\sigma^{m\dot\alpha\alpha}P_m,\qquad [Q^i_\alpha,Q^j_\beta]=0,\qquad [\bar Q_{\dot\alpha i},\bar Q_{\dot\beta j}]=0,

Lemma 8.4 is the semigroup property of this exact renormalisation-group flow and its compatibility with the BV differential.
Physics notation (the equivariant quantum master equation).
$I_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}[T]$ is the Wilsonian effective action at scale $T$ with the constant superconformal ghosts.

(8.6) is the regularised Slavnov–Taylor identity: its arity-zero part is that of BRST invariance, its arity-one part along $x$ the Ward identity of the generator $x$, its arity-two part the closure of the algebra.

Physics notation (anomaly and renormalisation ambiguities).

$\mathrm{Ob}$ is the one-loop anomaly of the regularised Slavnov–Taylor and superconformal Ward identities; (i) is its Wess–Zumino consistency condition, (ii) states that it is removed by a finite counterterm exactly when it is $s$-exact, and (iii) identifies the finite renormalisation ambiguities with $H^0$ of $s$ on local cochains, the field redefinitions being trivial.

In (iv) the coupling direction is a finite renormalisation of the coupling: through the pairing $(X,Y)=-\tfrac{4\hbar}{g^2}\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ the action $S$ is proportional to $g^{-2}$ at fixed $\mathfrak g$-valued fields, and $\mu S$ is $S$ with $g^{-2}\mapsto\mu g^{-2}$.
$G_B$ is the relative normalisation of $Q$ and $\bar Q$ (Theorem 8.20 (ii)).

$B$ is the $\mathfrak u(1)$ outer automorphism of $\mathfrak{psu}(2,2|4)$, the hypercharge $U(1)_Y$: in $\mathfrak{gl}(4|4)$, with real form $\mathfrak u(2,2|4)$, it is the commutator with $\operatorname{diag}(0_4,1_4)$.

Proposition 8.10 states that this ambiguity, a relative rescaling of $Q$ and $\bar Q$, is independent of the finite renormalisation of the coupling.
Physics notation (the one-loop generators).

$Q_1(O)^\alpha{}_i$, $\bar Q_1(O)^{\dot\alpha i}$, $S_1(O)_\alpha{}^i$, $\bar S_1(O)_{\dot\alpha i}$ are the one-loop corrections to the transformations of $O$ under $Q^i_\alpha$, $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha i}$, $S^\alpha{}_i$, $\bar S^{\dot\alpha i}$; $P_1$, $M_1$, $R_1$, $K_1$, $D_1$ are those under $P_b$, $\mathfrak{so}(4)$, $\mathfrak{su}(4)_R$, $K_b$, $\Delta$; $\hbar L_1(O)^{(0)}$ is the one-loop correction to the BRST variation of $O$.
For the physics dilatation $D=-E=-\tfrac12\Delta$ (the generator $-E$ of [SW, (3)]), acting through $-\Lambda^{(1)}$ (Corollary 8.17), the one-loop dilatation operator is $\tfrac12D_1$.

For every $\theta$, the coefficients of $O$ in $\tfrac12D_1(O)$ for the Konishi operator and for the $\mathbf{20'}$ differ by $\tfrac{3g^2N}{4\pi^2}$.

For $\mathfrak{su}(N)$, on the part with two external scalars, (9.16) reads $P_1(O)=\big(\tfrac13+\theta_P\big)\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}\,b^m\partial_mO$, a one-loop multiple of the classical translation: the term $\tfrac13$ comes from the cycles in which $S^{(1)}(P_b)$ appears as the composite $A_m$–$c$ line $2\big(\partial_b(P\star)^2\otimes1\big)K_0$, with the derivative $\partial_b$ in place of the dilatation vertex, and $\theta_P$ from the finite counterterm $\theta_P$ units times $\sum_I\int d^4x\,(b^m\partial_mA_I,A^*_I)$.

The components of this chapter are computed at $T=\infty$ and are the same at every finite endpoint $T$ of the transfer (Remark 9.35, Theorem 8.15 (ii)); the composite line is of order $|p|^{-3}$ at small momentum, $|x-y|^{-1}$ in position space.
Physics notation (letters and composite operators).

A letter is one constituent field of a composite operator with its derivatives, in the components of the physics notation key after Section 1.2: $\partial^\alpha c$, $\partial^\alpha A_m$, $\partial^\alpha A_I$ (equivalently $\partial^\alpha A_{ij}$ in the antisymmetric $\mathbf 6$ of $SU(4)$), $\partial^\alpha\lambda_\alpha{}^i$ (undotted, $S_+$, in the $\mathbf 4$), $\partial^\alpha\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}$ (dotted, $S_-$, in the $\bar{\mathbf 4}$), and the antifields $\partial^\alpha A^*_m$, $\partial^\alpha A^*_{ij}$, $\partial^\alpha\lambda^{*\alpha}{}_i$, $\partial^\alpha\bar\lambda^{*\dot\alpha i}$, $\partial^\alpha c^*$.
Its Weyl weight is its canonical mass dimension (block after Definition 6.1) and its degree is its ghost number (key).

A gauge-invariant operator is a polynomial in the covariant letters $D^nF_{mn}$, $D^nA_I$, $D^n\lambda$, $D^n\bar\lambda$, the letters of [B03c, Table 1]; written in the letters of this chapter, each covariant derivative $D_m=\partial_m+[A_m,-]$ contributes letters $A_m$ with fewer derivatives, so a covariant letter is a sum of monomials of ordinary letters.
The pair weight of two letters is the sum of their canonical dimensions.
Physics notation (one-loop renormalisation acts on pairs of fields).

Theorem 10.4 is the statement that the one-loop divergence of a composite operator is the sum over the pairs of its constituent fields of the Wick contraction of the pair with the propagator in the background of all fields, the propagator dressed by any number of insertions of the interaction vertices; the remaining fields are spectators.
This is the two-body form of the one-loop dilatation operator, which acts on two letters at a time [B03c, (2.12), (2.16)].

The term $k=0$ is the self-contraction of the two fields, a pure power divergence (the normal-ordering term), and the graphs in which the operator sits on a tree are the field-strength and coupling renormalisation of the action (Chapter 4), which carry no counterterm of the operator.
The graphs of the scalar bilinears are those of the block after Proposition 5.13.
Physics notation (colour factors and the planar limit).

For $\mathfrak{su}(N)$ with $(X,Y)=-\tfrac{4\hbar}{g^2}\operatorname{tr}(XY)$, $\kappa=-\tfrac{4\hbar}{g^2}$, and with the fields $X=-igX^aT^a$ of the key, $(-,-)^{-1}=2\kappa^{-1}\sum_aT^a\otimes T^a$ for $\operatorname{tr}(T^aT^b)=\tfrac12\delta^{ab}$, and the rules of Lemma 10.8 (ii) are the familiar contraction identity $\sum_a(T^a)_{ij}(T^a)_{kl}=\tfrac12\big(\delta_{il}\delta_{jk}-\tfrac1N\delta_{ij}\delta_{kl}\big)$ applied to the propagator of the pair.

The term with $N\operatorname{tr}(M_1Y_1\cdots Y_r)$ is the planar contraction of two neighbouring letters of a single trace, of order $g^2N$ in the unit $-\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}$; the other terms split the trace or are suppressed by $\tfrac1N$, the non-planar part of the one-loop dilatation operator.
In terms of the 't Hooft coupling $g^2N$ the unit is $-\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}$.
Physics notation (power divergences and operator mixing).
The proper-time cutoff $\varepsilon$ has dimension length$^2$, and $\varepsilon^{-1/2}$ is the momentum cutoff (block after Section 6.1).

The coefficient of $\varepsilon^{-m}$ is a power divergence $\propto\varepsilon^{-m}$, a mixing of the pair into composite operators of dimension lower by $2m$, and the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ a logarithmic divergence, a mixing into operators of the same dimension, the source of the anomalous dimensions.

The bound on the number of output fields is dimensional analysis together with ghost-number conservation: a pair of total dimension $w$ and ghost number $d$ mixes into at most $w+d$ fields; for example $(\partial_m\lambda_\alpha{}^i,\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha j})$, of dimension $4$ and ghost number $0$, mixes into at most four fields, with power divergences up to $\varepsilon^{-2}$.

In the canonical normalisation of the key ($A_m=-igA^a_mT^a$, $A_I=-igA^a_IT^a$), a term of a pair kernel with $r$ output fields multiplies the operator by $-\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}(-ig)^{r-2}$ times a number: order $g^2$ for two outputs and $g^3$ for three, the length-changing terms of the spin-chain picture.
At two loops at most three fields are contracted (Remark 10.14).
Physics notation (the Slavnov–Taylor identity of operator renormalisation).

$Q+\{I,-\}$ is the BRST variation $s$ on functionals of the fields and the BV differential with the BRST sources $A^*_m$, $A^*_{ij}$, $\lambda^{*\alpha}{}_i$, $\bar\lambda^{*\dot\alpha i}$, $c^*$ (block after Section 6.3).

Theorem 10.16 states that the logarithmic counterterm of the BRST variation of an operator is the BRST variation of its logarithmic counterterm, up to the field-strength renormalisation of the constituent fields (the block after Lemma 6.7): the one-loop Slavnov–Taylor identity of composite-operator renormalisation.

Twice the map of the theorem is the one-loop anomalous-dimension operator in the Callan–Symanzik sense of Theorem 6.11 (block after that theorem): twice the logarithmic operator counterterm plus the wave-function renormalisation $\gamma_{A_I}=\gamma_{A_m}=\frac{g^2N}{8\pi^2}$, $\gamma_\lambda=\frac{g^2N}{4\pi^2}$, $\gamma_c=\frac{g^2N}{16\pi^2}$ of the letters (block after Section 6.4).

(W1) is the statement for one field, (W2) for two, and Proposition 10.19 says that the BRST identity completes the outputs into covariant combinations, $\partial_m\to D_m=\partial_m+[A_m,-]$ and $\partial_mA_n-\partial_nA_m\to F_{mn}$, once the part with fewer fields is known.
Physics notation (Feynman parameters and the regularisation scheme).
$\alpha_j=t_j/\sum_it_i$ are the Feynman parameters of the one-loop graph, the centre $-\sum_j\alpha_jq_j$ is the shift of the loop momentum that completes the square, and the momentum form $\sum_{i

The regulator cuts every Schwinger proper time at $t_e\ge\varepsilon$, which in Feynman parameters is the cutoff $\tau\ge\varepsilon/\min_e\alpha_e$ on the total proper time; Proposition 10.23 states that the logarithmic divergence, and with it every anomalous dimension, is the same for any cutoff shape, while the power divergences and the finite parts are scheme dependent.
All coefficients are rational: Beta-type integrals of polynomials in the Feynman parameters.
Physics notation (point splitting and the distribution of derivatives).

The generating function places the two fields at $x+y_a$ and $x+y_b$; the coefficient of $y_a^\alpha y_b^\beta/\alpha!\beta!$ is the kernel of the pair $(\partial^\alpha\varphi_a,\partial^\beta\varphi_b)$, so the derivatives of the two letters are redistributed over the outputs by the Feynman-parameter integrals $\int_0^1\alpha^{n_1+j}(1-\alpha)^{n_2+j}d\alpha=\frac{(n_1+j)!\,(n_2+j)!}{(n_1+n_2+2j+1)!}$.

In Beisert's harmonic action [B03c, (4.27)–(4.29)] the two-site Hamiltonian redistributes the oscillators of two letters with the coefficients $(-1)^{1+n_{12}n_{21}}\Gamma(\tfrac12(n_{12}+n_{21}))\Gamma(1+\tfrac12(n-n_{12}-n_{21}))/\Gamma(1+\tfrac12n)$, also Beta functions, with the diagonal value $h(\tfrac n2)$; on the $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ sector it reduces to $H'_{12}$ of [B03c, (3.14)], which Proposition 10.34 reproduces on two sites from these integrals summed over the chains.

For the quartic bubble, a pair $(\partial_\mu\phi,\partial_ u\phi)$ of scalars is replaced by $ rac{\hbar}{16\pi^2}\log\varepsilon ig(- frac16\partial_\mu\partial_ u- frac1{12}\delta_{\mu u}\partial^2 ig)$ of the product of the two outputs (Example 10.28).
Physics notation (the bosonic pair kernels in components).

In the tables, $a_1$, $a_2$ are the polarisations of the two letters and $b_j$ those of the outputs: $(a_1,b_1)=a_{1m}b_{1m}$ for gluons and $\tfrac14a_1^{ij}b_{1ij}=a_{1I}b_{1I}$ for scalars, and $ip_j=\partial$ on the $j$-th output field.

For example the rows of $(A_I,A_J)$ with the outputs $(A_K,A_L)$ are the gluon-exchange triangle (two cubic vertices joined by a gluon line, coefficient $2\delta_{IK}\delta_{JL}$) and the quartic scalar vertex ($-2\delta_{IJ}\delta_{KL}-2\delta_{IK}\delta_{JL}+4\delta_{IL}\delta_{JK}$), each times the colour factor of the table; their sum gives the $SO(6)$ density of Proposition 10.31.
Remark 10.50 gives the remaining two-component forms.
Physics notation (the $SO(6)$ spin chain).

With $\gamma=2\times$(the map) the anomalous dimension (Theorem [10.16](#c10-02027)) and the unit $-\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}$, Proposition [10.31](#c10-02152) is the one-loop dilatation operator of the scalar sector,
\gamma=\frac{g^2N}{8\pi^2}\sum_{l}\big(1-P_{l,l+1}+\tfrac12K_{l,l+1}\big),

the $SO(6)$ integrable spin chain of the scalar sector, with $P$ the permutation and $K$ the trace of the two neighbouring $SO(6)$ indices; in the $SU(4)$ form, $(A_{ij},A_{kl})\mapsto2A_{kl}A_{ij}-\tfrac12\varepsilon_{ijkl}A^{mn}A_{mn}$ in units.

It gives $0$ on the $\mathbf{20'}$ and $\frac{3g^2N}{4\pi^2}$ on the Konishi operator (block after Remark 6.13); on the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ sector of Proposition 10.32, with $Z=A_1+iA_2$, $X=A_3+iA_4$, it is $\frac{g^2N}{8\pi^2}$ times the Heisenberg Hamiltonian $\sum_l(1-P_{l,l+1})$, whose cyclic spectra are those of the table.
Physics notation (twist two and harmonic sums).

$n=(1,i,0,0)$ is a null vector of the complexified Euclidean space, the Wick image of a light-cone direction, and $(\iota_nd_{A|_V})^kZ=(n^mD_m)^kZ$ are the light-cone covariant derivatives of the complex scalar $Z=A_1+iA_2$; the operators $\operatorname{tr}\big((n\cdot D)^kZ\,(n\cdot D)^{S-k}Z\big)$ are the twist-two operators of the $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ sector.
The eigenvalues $-8h(S)$ of the map give the one-loop anomalous dimensions
\gamma(S)=\frac{g^2N}{2\pi^2}\sum_{j=1}^S\frac1j\qquad(S\ \text{even}),
the harmonic sums of [B03c, (2.31)]: $0$ for the $\mathbf{20'}$ descendants at $S=0$ and $\frac{3g^2N}{4\pi^2}$ at $S=2$, the Konishi multiplet.
Twist two needs the gluons inside the covariant derivatives: without the pairs $(A_m,Z)$ the value at $S=2$ would be $\frac{g^2N}{6\pi^2}$ instead of $\frac{3g^2N}{4\pi^2}$.
Physics notation (comparison with the one-loop dilatation operator).
[B03c, (1.2), (1.3)] writes the dilatation generator as $D(g)=D_0+\frac{g^2N}{8\pi^2}H+O(g^3)$, $H=\sum_lH_{l,l+1}$ with $H_{12}=2h(J_{12})$ the harmonic action on two neighbouring letters.

With the physics dilatation $D=-E=-\tfrac12\Delta$ (key), the one-loop part of $D$ on an operator is $\gamma$, twice the map of Theorem 10.16 (block after Theorem 6.11), and Corollary 10.35 is $\gamma=\frac{g^2N}{8\pi^2}H$ on the scalar, $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, $\mathfrak{su}(1|1)$ and twist-two sectors.

[B03c] fixes $H$ by $\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)$ invariance and a point-splitting computation in the $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ sector; here the same numbers come from the proper-time cutoff, and their agreement is the scheme independence of the one-loop spectrum.
Physics notation ($D_1$ and the anomalous dimensions).
On an operator of ghost number $0$ the physics dilatation acts through $-\Lambda^{(1)}(D)=\tfrac12\Lambda^{(1)}(\Delta)$, so its one-loop part is $\tfrac12D_1$.

On an eigen-operator $\tfrac12D_1O=\gamma_OO$, with $\gamma_O$ twice the eigenvalue of the map of Theorem 10.16, when the composite term minus the bracket of $O$ with $\hbar F_1^{(1)}(\Delta)$ beyond the field-strength renormalisation vanishes on cohomology; on the part with scalar outputs of the planar scalar sector this difference is $-(\tfrac13+\theta)$ units times $\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),O\}$, which vanishes at the value $\theta=-\tfrac13$ fixed by the arity-two equation (Theorem 9.31).

The one-body terms of the table are twice the gauge-dependent wave-function renormalisations of the letters in Feynman gauge plus the finite counterterm of the dilatation vertex beyond the field-counting functional, and the composite term is the contribution of the line from $c$ to $A_m$ through the dilatation vertex that exists because $(Q^{GF})^2\neq0$ in Feynman gauge (block after Section 9.2).
$v.X=2(x^m\partial_m+w_X)X$ is twice the classical scale transformation of the letter.
Physics notation (the planar scalar sector).

For $\operatorname{tr}(A_{I_1}\cdots A_{I_L})$ at large $N$, on the part with scalar outputs, $\tfrac12D_1=\frac{g^2N}{8\pi^2}\sum_l\big(1-P_{l,l+1}+\tfrac12K_{l,l+1}\big)-\tfrac12\big(\tfrac13+\theta\big)\big(-\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}\big)\cdot2\big(x^m\partial_m+L\big)$: the $SO(6)$ chain plus a multiple of the classical scale transformation, which vanishes at $\theta=-\tfrac13$.

$P_1$ is the one-loop correction to the translation $P_m=\partial_m$ on operators; it is the multiple $-(\tfrac13+\theta_P)\big(-\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}\big)\partial_b$ of the classical translation, and the finite operator renormalisation $O\mapsto O+\tfrac a2\cdot2(x^m\partial_m+w_O)O$ of Proposition 9.34, $a$ a multiple of the unit, a position-dependent rescaling of the operator, removes it without changing the anomalous dimensions.
Physics notation (one-loop corrections to the superconformal generators).

$Q_1$, $S_1$, $K_1$ are the one-loop corrections to the action of the supercharges $Q^i_\alpha$, $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha i}$, the special supercharges $S^\alpha{}_i$, $\bar S^{\dot\alpha i}$ and the special conformal generators on composite operators (block after Definition 8.16); by Proposition 10.45 each is a two-body plus a one-body operator on the letters, like the dilatation operator.

A supercharge raises the dimension by $\tfrac12$, so its two-body kernel on a pair of total dimension $w$ and ghost number $d$ has dimension $w+\tfrac12$ and at most $w+\tfrac12+d$ output fields, and the special supercharges and special conformal generators, which carry the position $x$, lower the dimension by $\tfrac12$ and $1$ and may contain $x$ once and twice.

In the canonical normalisation the terms of the supercharges of order $g$ that change the number of fields, from the commutator terms of $F_A$ in $\tfrac12(\rho(F_A)\xi,\lambda^*)$, belong to the classical $S^{(1)}(\xi)$ (block after Definition 2.12), and the one-loop components start at order $g^2N$, a term with $r$ outputs from a pair carrying $g^r$ as in the block after Proposition 10.12.

The second-order operator on pairs of letters of the holomorphic twist [BK, (3.7)] is to be compared with the two-body part of the twisted one-loop differential of Chapter 8, which contains $Q_1$ along a square-zero supercharge (block after Section 8.6).
Physics notation (the composite line along $D$ and $P_m$).

The composite kernel is the line of the block after Section 9.2: the gauge propagator $\langle A_mA_n\rangle$, the classical scale transformation $(2x^n\partial_n+2)A_m$ of the gauge field inserted on it, and the line $\langle A^*_m\,c\rangle$, which in the gauge-fixed language is the ghost propagator joined to the antighost derivative $\partial_m\bar c$ that replaces the BRST source $A^*_m$ in Feynman gauge.
Along a translation $P_m=\partial_m$ the inserted transformation is $b^n\partial_nA_m$.

In momentum space the two propagators of the same momentum give the factor $e^{-2\varepsilon p^2}/p^4$ of the square kernel, so the line runs from a ghost $c$ to a gauge field $A_m$ and behaves as $|p|^{-3}$ at small momentum.

It exists because the Feynman-gauge fixing and the conformal transformation of the gauge field do not commute, $(Q^{GF})^2\neq0$; along the R-symmetry rotations it vanishes, the ghost being an R-singlet.

The sector parts of $S^{(1)}(\Delta)$ and $S^{(1)}(P_b)$ are the scale transformation and the translation of the three field types separately: the scalars $A_I$, the gauginos $\lambda_\alpha{}^i,\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}$, and the gauge field with the ghost.
Physics notation (regulator insertions and the composite pair kernel).

The special edge is the difference between the regularised and the bare contraction of a field with its BRST source, $e^{-\varepsilon p^2}-1$ times the field–source delta function: the regulator insertion by which the regularised BRST variation fails to be a derivation (block after Theorem 4.30).

A special-edge composite cycle is a one-loop graph through two constituent fields of a composite operator with one dilatation or translation insertion on the ghost–gauge line and one regulator insertion.
The regulator insertion lives at proper times $t\le\varepsilon$, so the graph is a pure short-distance contribution: powers $\varepsilon^{-m}$, a finite part and no $\log\varepsilon$.

The finite part is the composite pair kernel, a finite local two-body contribution of the gauge-fixing sector to the one-loop action of the dilatation and of the translations on composite operators; with the proper-time cutoff $\varepsilon^{-1/2}$ playing the role of the momentum cutoff (block after Proposition 10.12), its value depends on the shape of the cutoff and is a scheme-dependent number.
Physics notation (locality of the gauge-fixing contribution).

In a Feynman-gauge computation of the one-loop scale transformation of a gauge-invariant composite operator, the graphs with the dilatation insertion on an internal gauge line split into graphs through two constituent fields and self-energy-type graphs on one field.
The latter contain the composite two-point function, nonlocal on $A_m$, $\lambda$, $\bar\lambda$ and $c$ through $\log p^2$ of the field momentum (block after Theorem 9.25).

For a BRST-invariant operator the Slavnov–Taylor identity cancels these nonlocal terms against the graphs through pairs, and the whole insertion becomes the sum over pairs of constituent fields of the finite parts of the graphs with one regulator insertion: a local two-body operator, of the same form as the one-loop dilatation operator acting on neighbouring letters [B03c, (2.12)].
The one-body part of the one-loop dilatation is then the field-strength renormalisation of the letters together with the finite counterterm of the dilatation, as in the block after Theorem 10.38.
Physics notation (the finite renormalisations of the scale transformation).
$\hbar F_1^{(1)}(\Delta)$ is the finite local counterterm of the dilatation.

Up to BRST-exact field redefinitions its free quadratic part is a combination of the classical scale transformations $\varphi\mapsto(2x^m\partial_m+2w_\varphi)\varphi$ of the three field types, with the coefficients $\theta$ for the scalars $A_I$, $\theta_\lambda$ for the gauginos and $\theta_V$ for the gauge field with the ghost.
Such a term changes the one-loop dilatation of a letter by a multiple of its classical scale transformation, a multiple of $x^m\partial_m+w$, and leaves the anomalous dimensions unchanged.

Without reflection invariance the list has one further entry, the rotation $\lambda_\alpha{}^i\mapsto e^{i\varphi}\lambda_\alpha{}^i$, $\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}\mapsto e^{-i\varphi}\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha i}$ of the free gaugino, which is odd under the reflection of the Euclidean theory (block after Theorem 9.25).
Physics notation (the commutator of $D$ and $P_m$ at one loop).
With the physics dilatation $D=-E=-\tfrac12\Delta$ (key), the arity-two equation along $(\Delta,P_b)$ is the one-loop form of $[D,P_m]=P_m$ on composite operators, up to BRST-exact terms.

In a scheme in which the translations act classically, it states that the part of the one-loop dilatation that is proportional to the position, $x^m$ times a one-loop translation, is BRST exact: the one-loop dilatation of an operator at the point $x$ is its anomalous-dimension operator, with no further term in $x^m\partial_m$.

This condition fixes the coefficients $\theta$, $\theta_\lambda$, $\theta_V$ of the scale transformations in the finite counterterm, one for each field type, by requiring that the multiple of $x^m\partial_m$ produced by the gauge-fixing graphs cancel.
Physics notation (the light-cone families and the universal density).

$n^m$ with $n^2=0$ is a light-cone direction, $D_n=n^mD_m$ is the light-cone covariant derivative $D_+$, $\psi=\lambda_1{}^i$ is the $+$ component of a Weyl gaugino, and $F_{11}$ is the self-dual field-strength component $F_{++}$; the letters are the covariant letters $D_+^kZ$, $D_+^k\psi$, $D_+^kF_{++}$ of the block after Definition 10.1.

The families are the light-cone $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ sectors of [B03c]: the twist-two scalar operators $\operatorname{tr}(D_+^kZ\,D_+^{S-k}Z)$, the gaugino operators $\operatorname{tr}(D_+^k\psi\,D_+^{S-k}\psi)$ and the gluon operators $\operatorname{tr}(D_+^kF_{++}\,D_+^{S-k}F_{++})$, whose one-loop anomalous dimensions are the harmonic sums $\gamma=\frac{g^2N}{2\pi^2}h(j)$ with $j=S$, $S+1$, $S+2$ [B03c, (2.31)], together with the $\mathfrak{su}(1|1)$ sector of $Z$ and one gaugino component and two mixed families.

The theorem says that, on two neighbouring fields of a single trace, the gauge-fixing contribution acts as $-\tfrac43$ units times the identity on the same ordering, with no exchange and no trace term, plus $-\tfrac16$ units times the derivative of the pair along the translation: a universal multiple of the classical scaling, $-\tfrac23$ units for each field and each derivative.
Physics notation (anomalous dimensions and the absent one-loop translation).

The one-loop dilatation is $\tfrac12D_1$ (block after Definition 8.16), so on the families $\tfrac12D_1=\gamma$ with $\gamma=\frac{g^2N}{8\pi^2}E$ and $E$ an eigenvalue of Beisert's one-loop Hamiltonian $\sum_lH_{l,l+1}$, $H_{12}=2h(J_{12})$: $\gamma=\frac{g^2N}{2\pi^2}h(S)$ on twist two, $\gamma=\frac{3g^2N}{4\pi^2}$ on the Konishi multiplet, which contains the trace scalar bilinear, $\operatorname{tr}(F_{++}F_{++})$ and the $\mathfrak{su}(1|1)$ state $\operatorname{tr}(Z\psi\psi)$, and $\frac{g^2N}{8\pi^2}$ times the spectra of the $\mathfrak{su}(1|1)$ table.

In the translation-covariant scheme $P_1=0$: the translations act on composite operators without a one-loop correction, $[P_m,O(x)]=\partial_mO(x)$, and the finite operator renormalisation of the block after Section 9.5 is not needed.
Physics notation (the special supercharges from the supercharges).

Classically the special supercharges $S^\alpha{}_i$, $\bar S^{\dot\alpha i}$ act on an operator at the point $x$ as the supercharges with the position-dependent parameter $\rho(x)\eta$, whose two-component form is $-i\,x_m\sigma^m_{\alpha\dot\alpha}\bar\eta^{\dot\alpha i}$ and $i\,x_m\eta^\alpha{}_i\sigma^m_{\alpha\dot\alpha}$, plus a term at the point: this is the content of the commutators $[P_m,S]\propto\sigma_m\bar Q$ and $[P_m,\bar S]\propto\sigma_mQ$ (Proposition 2.4).

The proposition is the one-loop form of these commutators: when the one-loop translation vanishes, the position-dependent part of the one-loop special supercharge is the one-loop supercharge with the parameter $\rho(b)\eta$, and the one-loop special supercharge of an operator at the origin is the new datum.
For the scalar bilinears, for which no such term at the point exists (block after Corollary 7.15), the one-loop $S$ is fixed by the one-loop $Q$.
The one-loop $K_m$ is fixed by the one-loop $P_m$ and the one-loop normalisation of the two-point functions through $K=P^\dagger$ (Corollary 8.41).
Physics notation (the half-BPS bilinears of the twist).

For a rank-one supercharge $Q^i_\alpha u^\alpha z_i$-type, such as the supercharge $Q^4_-$ of [BK] and [CY13, (2.1)], the scalars with $\rho(w)\xi=0$ are the three complex scalars $A_{ij}z^j$, the letters $\gamma^I\sim\Phi^{4I}$ of [BK, (3.51)], annihilated by $Q$ classically.
Their symmetric traceless bilinears $\operatorname{tr}(\gamma^{(I}\gamma^{J)})$ are half-BPS chiral primaries in the $\mathbf{20'}$ (block after Section 9.4).

The proposition states that their one-loop $Q$-variation vanishes identically, at every order at which the selection rules of the block after Proposition 7.13 hold, which is the untwisted form of $Q_1(\gamma^I\gamma^J)=0$ [BK, (3.77)].
Physics notation (the twisted one-loop supercharge and the Konishi entry).

The twisted differential $Q^\xi_0+\hbar Q^\xi_1$ is the action of a single Poincar'e supercharge $Q$ of rank one on composite operators, classically and at one loop, and its cohomology at $\hbar^0$ is the space of classically $\tfrac1{16}$-BPS operators [CY13].

The one-loop part acts on pairs of letters [BK, (3.7)] and raises the dimension by $\tfrac12$, a two-site operator of order $g^2N$ in the canonical normalisation with the leg count of the order-$g^2$ two-site terms of the $\mathfrak{su}(2|3)$ supercharge of [B03] (block after Section 10.9).

The individual pair entries of [BK, (3.64)–(3.69)] depend on the normalisation of the operators: the Konishi entry, the one-loop term that maps the pair of a gaugino and a scalar to $\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha}\bar\lambda^{\dot\alpha}$, is the twisted form of the one-loop Konishi anomaly, and its coefficient moves when the cubic scalar operator in the classical $Q$-variation is mixed with the operator $\operatorname{tr}(\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha}\bar\lambda^{\dot\alpha})$ of the same quantum numbers.
